elements.element: Customer is not subject to any non-compete restriction.
elements.evidence: Rendered §12.3 states that nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service and expressly confirms that Customer has made no non-compete commitment. The restrictive §12.4 is absent.

elements.element: Customer is not subject to any field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Rendered §12.3 expressly permits Customer to conduct business in any field or territory.

elements.element: Any restriction is limited to a specifically named competing product.
elements.evidence: No restriction remains in the rendered clause, so there is no broader or unnamed-product restriction.

elements.element: Any restriction applies only during the agreement term.
elements.evidence: No restriction remains during or after the term; the former 24-month post-term restriction has been deleted.

elements.element: Any restriction is capped at 12 months.
elements.evidence: No restriction remains, so no restriction exceeds the 12-month cap.

elements.element: Any restriction includes a carve-out for Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: Rendered §12.3 affirmatively states that nothing restricts Customer from developing any product or service, which fully protects internal development.

elements.element: Any restriction includes a carve-out for acquisitions.
elements.evidence: Rendered §12.3 affirmatively states that nothing restricts Customer from acquiring any product or service.

result.reason: The rendered clause achieves the preferred position by deleting §12.4 entirely while retaining §12.3's express confirmation that Customer has no non-compete, exclusivity, or field-of-use restriction. Because no restriction remains, the narrower fallback limitations are also satisfied. The change is minimal and resolves the contradiction between former §12.4 and §12.3 without altering unrelated operative terms.
